title: Define latency sweep windows and graceful-degradation policy for multiplexed requests
creator: Sasha Patel
description: Establish operational definitions, acceptance criteria, and rollout gates for a new latency sweep window mechanism and a tenant-aware graceful-degradation policy targeting multiplexed request patterns (long-lived multiplexed connections such as streaming or conversational multiplexing). This ticket captures the product requirements, evaluation metric set, and canary gating rules required for release into hosted and dedicated modes.
motivation: Multiplexed request patterns (client multiplexing multiple conversational sessions over a single connection or interleaved streaming) have different latency tail characteristics and cache hit behavior. Existing SLOs optimize single-request tails and do not account for per-connection resource contention or prefix-KV cache pressure. Without explicit sweep windows and degradation policies, we see intermittent P99 regressions during tenant surges and maintenance windows which cause customer escalations and higher error budgets burn rate.
scope: Define latency sweep windows, degradation bands, tenant priority weighting, canary gating rules, and monitoring signals required for rollout. Produce acceptance criteria and an operator playbook. Work with Eng to implement probe traffic and runtime flags to enable controlled canaries.
out_of_scope: Implementation changes to the low-level kernel scheduling logic and model quantization profiles; separate tickets should handle kernel-level optimizations and quantization acceptance matrices.
acceptance_criteria: SLO definitions: For multiplexed requests the service will target p95 <= 180ms, p99 <= 650ms for interactive responses under normal load; during sweep windows define two degradation bands with clear triggers.
Availability target: 99.95% regional availability for multiplexed endpoints (same as standard API) with documented deviation handling during maintenance windows.
Error budget policy: Define separate error budget counter for multiplexed workload class with automated throttling start at 30% error budget burn over a 1h sliding window.

Canary gating: New behavior can be enabled for 1% sample of traffic for 24h; to promote to 10% must pass: no >10% relative increase in p99, error rate delta <0.02, and no customer-impacting alerts beyond informational level.
Operator playbook: Runbook that lists precise steps for toggling sweep windows, reverting tenant weights, and invoking fallback routing to low-cost variants.

Observability: Dashboards with multiplexed-specific metrics (per-connection concurrency, kv-cache-hit-rate-by-tenant, p95/p99 by connection-length bin) and predefined alert thresholds exist and are validated with synthetic probes.

CI/QA: Regression test harness includes synthetic multiplexed load scenarios that exercise boundary conditions (burst connect/disconnect, sustained multi-session traffic) and is green in release pipeline.
Documentation: Console docs updated with new SLO semantics and guidance for customers configuring tenant priority lanes and maintenance windows.
Signoffs: Product, Runtime Engineering, SRE, and Support have signed off on acceptance criteria and runbook.
Updated SLA wording (customer-facing) drafted and reviewed by legal for any change to advertised availability tied to scheduled sweep windows.
rollout_gates: Gate 0 - Unit/Integration: All runtime flags compile and unit tests pass; synthetic probe harness run locally.
Gate 1 - Internal Canary (1%): Enable on non-customer test tenants for 24h; require stability: p99 delta < +8% vs control and kv-cache-hit-rate degradation < 5%.
Gate 2 - Small Customer Canary (10%): Select low-risk tenants, monitor for 48h; require no pager incidents and error budget burn rate within configured threshold.
Gate 3 - Gradual Ramp (25->50->100): Each step 24h with automated rollback if rolling averages violate SLOs: p99 > 1.15x baseline for more than 1h or error rate spike > 0.05 absolute.
Automatic rollback triggers: sustained kv-cache-hit-rate drop >10% OR per-tenant tail latency spike > +100ms for >30m OR critical customer impact alerts from Support.
Manual gates: SRE must confirm resource headroom and Eng must validate no goroutine/worker-leak regressions before region-wide enable.
Maintenance window handling: Allow scheduled sweep windows to be annotated per-region with explicit start/end and a pre-announced degradation SLA for customers.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics to emit: multiplex.connection_count, multiplex.sessions_per_connection, multiplex.kv_cache_hit_rate_by_tenancy, multiplex.p95_ms, multiplex.p99_ms, multiplex.stream_rebuffer_count
Dashboards: multiplex:overview, multiplex:per-tenant-slo, multiplex:canary-comparison - links added to PRD
Alerts: alert if multiplex.p99_ms > 1.2x baseline for 15m, or if kv_cache_hit_rate_by_tenancy drops >8% for 10m
Burn-rate alert: automated throttle triggers when multiplex error budget burn reaches 30% in 1h or 60% in 24h.
implementation_notes: Runtime flag: feature.multiplex.sweep_windows (boolean) + feature.multiplex.tenant_weight (map via config service).
Engineering tasks: probe traffic generator for multiplexed workloads (ENG-50411), per-tenant telemetry tagging (ENG-50412), canary infra plumbing (ENG-50413).
Data needed for acceptance: 2 weeks of baseline multiplex telemetry from production (p95/p99 buckets by connection length) and regression harness results.
Estimate: changes span runtime, router, and console; expect a cross-functional 3-sprint effort with parallel work streams.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Sweep windows cause oscillation in routing (thrashing) if thresholds too tight. Mitigation: introduce hysteresis and minimum hold time of 15 minutes before route changes.

Risk: Tenant weighting could unfairly deprioritize high-value customers. Mitigation: default behavior is conservative; require explicit customer opt-in for low-priority shunting and PM/AE review for any changes affecting billed SLA.
Risk: Observability gaps hide regressions. Mitigation: mandatory synthetic probe runs during each gate and cross-check with Cost/Latency telemetry in Console.
